record.original_question: Given a finite-dimensional Lie group G, determine whether G admits a left-invariant Hessian structure.

evidence.quote: Left invariant Hessian structure in a ﬁnite dimensional Lie group G

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. A Hessian structure on $G$ is a pair $(
abla, g)$ consisting of a flat torsion-free affine connection $
abla$ and a Riemannian metric $g$ such that, locally around every point, there exists a smooth function $\varphi$ for which $g = 
abla d\varphi$ (equivalently, in $
abla$-affine coordinates $x^1, \dots, x^n$, one has $g_{ij} = \partial^2 \varphi / \partial x^i \partial x^j$). The structure $(
abla, g)$ is called left-invariant if both $
abla$ and $g$ are invariant under all left translations $L_a : G 	o G$, $a \in G$.

Determine, for an arbitrary finite-dimensional Lie group $G$, necessary and sufficient conditions on $G$ (equivalently, on its Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$) that guarantee the existence of a left-invariant Hessian structure on $G$. In particular, give a complete characterization (classification) of those Lie algebras $\mathfrak{g}$ which admit a Hessian structure compatible with the left-invariant framework above.
artifact.category_tag: Left-invariant Hessian structures on Lie groups
artifact.status_search_result: Left-invariant Hessian structures can exist only on solvable Lie groups, but not every solvable Lie group admits one. A complete classification of Lie groups (or Lie algebras) admitting a left-invariant Hessian structure is not known; recent work (e.g., 2024–2025 arXiv preprints on moduli spaces of left-invariant statistical/Hessian structures) continues to address partial classifications, indicating the general existence/classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The moduli spaces of left-invariant statistical structures on Lie groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on classifying left-invariant Hessian/statistical structures on Lie groups, indicating the general classification is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of Lie groups admitting left-invariant Hessian structures is still an active topic.

status_evidence.title: Flat left-invariant connections adapted to the automorphism structure
status_evidence.snippet: Classical work showing flat left-invariant connections (a prerequisite for Hessian structures) impose strong constraints, related to solvability.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of left-invariant flat structures, a prerequisite for Hessian structures, is restrictive and not fully classified.
